Hi Ellen / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can lock down a recommended cost profile and next steps for a pilot:

Summary of what you asked for:
- Real-time summarization + entity extraction for support tickets (avg session = 6 messages)
- ~12k active daily users, expect 2.5 requests/user/day initially -> ~30k requests/day
- Typical request length: 120 tokens input, 80 tokens output (avg 200 tokens/request)
- Peak concurrency estimate: 120 concurrent requests during peak window (09:00–11:00 PT)
- Target economic goal: ~ $800–1,200 per 1M tokens (customer wants ballpark unit economics)

Clarifying asks (can you confirm?):
1) Are the 2.5 requests/user/day an average over 24h or concentrated in business hours (this affects batching/concurrency)?
2) Do you expect long multi-turn sessions where KV cache reuse will be high (>60% prefix reuse) or mostly independent one-off requests?
3) Any regulatory/data residency constraints beyond standard SOC2 needs?

Our initial costing assumptions (for planning):
- Workload model: continuous arrival with clear peaks. We'll assume 70% of requests occur within a 6-hour business window for pilot sizing.
- Avg tokens/day = 30k requests * 200 tokens = 6M tokens/day -> ~180M tokens/month.
- Continuous batching expectation: with steady arrival and 120 peak concurrency, we anticipate effective batch sizes of 8–16 on A100-equivalent pools with Redwood's continuous batching (lower latency SLOs target 150–250ms tail).
- Unit economics examples (rough ballparks for budgeting; exact depends on model, quant, and reserved capacity):
  * Hosted (on-demand) high-throughput model: $1,100 per 1M tokens
  * Dedicated medium-commit + 8-bit quantization: $680 per 1M tokens
  * Dedicated + KV cache reuse and prefix caching for sessions: effective cost could drop ~20–30% compared to stateless requests

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm Q1–Q3 above by EOD Friday so we can finalize a draft SOW and a pilot cost model?
- We'll follow up with a detailed cost spreadsheet (attached) and a one-hour technical deep-dive to validate concurrency and batching tradeoffs (suggest Wed next week).

Attachments: cost-model-1Mtokens.xlsx (ballpark calc), SOW-draft-streamline-20260310.pdf (initial outline)

Thanks — feel free to flag if any of the numbers above look off.

Hi team — small technical clarifications and what we'll validate in the deep-dive: 

- Continuous batching in Redwood groups inflight requests every 2–8ms window depending on configured latency SLOs; with your traffic profile and peak concurrency (~120–200), expected effective batch sizes are 10–18 for a single model shard. That keeps GPU utilization high while keeping tail latency controlled.
- For multi-turn sessions we expect significant KV cache reuse. We'll instrument a pilot to measure: cache hit rate, avg hidden state size, and token-per-request distribution. 60%+ cache reuse reduces compute per request substantially because prefix tokens don't require full attention recomputation when cached properly.
- Concurrency vs batching tradeoff: If you need strict 100–200ms p50 we recommend slightly smaller batching windows and more GPU shards (higher reserved capacity). If you can accept 200–300ms p50, batching windows can be wider yielding better unit economics.
- Spike handling: Redwood's smart routing can burst to additional shards and fall back to a lower-cost model variant for graceful degradation if reserved capacity hits hard limits — we'll model that scenario in the SOW.

I'll prepare a short deck for the technical deep-dive showing headroom vs cost for different SLOs.

-Rishi
